content.text:
Finding submitted.

## Summary

**Status: MISSING (critical)** — no vendor indemnity exists anywhere in this agreement.

**What I found**

The planner hint suggested a one-way indemnity running against us. The reality is worse in one sense and better in another: § 7 is captioned "LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; **INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR**," but the section body contains *no indemnity at all* — only a liability cap (7(a)), a consequential-damages waiver (7(b)), and a mutual attorneys' fees waiver (7(c)). A document-wide search for "indemnif" returns only the heading itself; "hold harmless" returns nothing. So there is no customer indemnity to narrow, and no vendor indemnity to expand.

**The gap that matters**

The only IP protection is § 5(c) (p0026), a bare non-infringement *warranty*. That is not a substitute for an indemnity: if a third party sues Clear Capital over the Works, RadialSpark has no obligation to defend us or fund the defence, and any warranty damages claim is capped at fees paid under § 7(a). § 7(c) even waives our fee recovery. That is the playbook's walk-away scenario — "no Vendor IP indemnity at all."

**A drafting tell worth flagging to the counterparty**

§ 7(a) carves "PARAGRAPH 9" out of Contractor's liability cap — but Paragraph 9 is *Independent Contractor status*, which generates no monetary obligation. This dangling cross-reference strongly suggests an indemnification clause once sat at Paragraph 9 and was lost in redrafting. That makes this an easy, non-adversarial ask: we are restoring something the document already assumes exists.

**The redline**

Inserted a new § 7(d) at the preferred position (IP infringement, breach of law, Contractor-caused data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a consent requirement on settlements that bind us. I also carved § 7(d) out of the § 7(a) cap and the § 7(c) fees waiver — without that, the indemnity would be self-defeating, since a defence obligation capped at fees paid is not a defence obligation. The comment offers the fallback (IP-only, usual exclusions, 3× annual fees super-cap) as a landing zone.

One note for your commercial judgment: the § 7(a) cap at "fees paid" and the § 7(c) fees waiver are independently weak, but I did not redline them here to avoid double-flagging the same commercial term — they belong to the limitation-of-liability rule.
